item.title: Longford & Roscommon two poorest counties in terms of disposable income
item.description: Longford and Roscommon are the poorest counties in Ireland in terms of disposable income. That's according to new statistics released by the CSO today. The county with the lowest disposable income per capita was Longford with an average of €23,725 per person. Longford is directly followed by Roscommon on the list with an average disposable income of €24,685 per person. item.title: Funeral arranged for Englishman who died after alleged assault in Ballaghaderreen
item.description: The funeral is taking place next week of an Englishman who died after an alleged assault in Ballaghaderreen. It’s taking place in Kent on February 12th. item.description: The Seanad has heard that water outages remain a problem in Cloonfad. He says they were unable to open for a day due to water outages last week. item.title: Calls for increased HAP thresholds
item.description: Calls have been made locally to increase thresholds for social applicants and applicants for the Housing Assistance Payments scheme. There are concerns that current income limits no longer reflect the financial pressures faced by many working individuals and families. As a result, some households are earning marginally above the thresholds yet remain unable to secure affordable accommodation in the private rental market. item.description: Plans to fast-track approval for a floating liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal have been met with growing concern from environmental groups and local representatives. item.title: Longford man told to pay €5,500 for careless driving causing serious bodily harm to 81-year-old
item.description: A Longford man has been ordered to pay a €500 fine and €5,000 in compensation for careless driving causing serious bodily harm to an 81-year-old man. The judge said it's lucky the pensioner wasn't killed. Longford Circuit Court today heard this crash happened between Edgeworthstown and Granard, in August 2024, shortly after 8 o'clock in the morning. item.title: 'More flesh on the bone' needed on Mulryan's Athlone masterplan - Taoiseach
item.description: The Taoiseach says more work needs to be done before plans to turn Athlone into a green city can fully progress. Developer Sean Mulryan and Ballymore hope to complete the project by 2040. Following a presentation to Roscommon councillors last month, Mulryan said the Government now needs to progress the plans.
